title: Pascal's Triangle

concept.title: Each row from the row above
body: In Pascal's triangle every row starts and ends with 1, and every other number is the **sum of the two numbers above it**: the one directly above-left and the one directly above-right. So a row can be computed from the previous row alone.

body.code:
row = [1]
for _ in range(n):
    print(*row)
    row = [1] + [row[i] + row[i + 1] for i in range(len(row) - 1)] + [1]

body: You only need to keep the current row in memory, not the whole triangle.

statement: Print the first `n` rows of Pascal's triangle. Row 1 is `1`, row 2 is `1 1`, row 3 is `1 2 1`, and so on.
outputFormat: Print `n` lines. Line `k` has `k` numbers separated by spaces.
hints: Each row begins and ends with 1.
A number in the middle is the sum of the two numbers above it in the previous row.
Keep only the previous row and build the next one from it.

explanation: The next row is built from the current one: the ends are 1 and each inner number is the sum of its two upper neighbours.

code.python:
n = int(input())

row = [1]
for _ in range(n):
    print(*row)
    row = [1] + [row[i] + row[i + 1] for i in range(len(row) - 1)] + [1]
